neighbours.label: Discusses the proteins and filament architecture of striated muscle, including troponin as a cardiac biomarker.
fire: Following prolonged chest discomfort, serum troponin concentrations rose sharply, indicating injury to cardiac muscle cells.
In pulmonary embolism, elevated troponin can accompany right ventricular strain despite unobstructed coronary arteries.
During skeletal muscle contraction, calcium binds troponin C, allowing tropomyosin to uncover binding sites on actin.
Within each sarcomere, thin actin filaments attach to Z discs while thick myosin filaments occupy the central region.
In relaxed muscle, tropomyosin obstructs the sites where myosin heads would otherwise attach to the thin filament.
Along the muscle fiber membrane, dystrophin links the intracellular contractile apparatus to a supporting complex of membrane proteins.
In processed beef, heating denatures myofibrillar and sarcoplasmic proteins, changing the texture and the ability to retain water.
As a skeletal fiber shortens, thick and thin filaments slide past each other, drawing the boundaries of each repeating unit closer.
quiet: After several hours of breathlessness, elevated natriuretic peptide concentrations suggested increased ventricular wall stress.
Among patients with pulmonary embolism, echocardiography may reveal right ventricular dilation and reduced systolic function.
Within skeletal muscle fibers, calcium released from intracellular stores raises the cytosolic concentration before force develops.
Under the microscope, skeletal muscle fibers appear as elongated multinucleated cells surrounded by delicate connective tissue.
In intestinal smooth muscle, calcium activates calmodulin, which stimulates phosphorylation and initiates contraction.
Beneath the erythrocyte membrane, spectrin organizes a flexible protein network that helps the cell withstand mechanical stress.
In refrigerated pork, salt concentration and tissue acidity influence tenderness, cooking losses, and the retention of water.
During proofreading of the laboratory manual, the editor changed troponin from bold lettering to italics throughout the alphabetical index.
